benchmark_categories.goal: Keep native graph work attributable and browser-visible geometry bounded at every scale tier.
benchmark_categories.metrics: UUID ingest, layout ticks, render-graph build, payload/export bytes, first paint and frame pacing
benchmark_categories.name: Graph render pipeline
benchmark_categories.why: GraphForge views need attributed ingest, layout, bounded geometry, payload, and export costs before browser paint.

benchmark_categories.goal: Beat Plotly/Bokeh/Altair on first interactive paint for common charts.
benchmark_categories.name: Small-data startup
benchmark_categories.why: Everyday charts should feel instant; a performance library cannot only win at 10M rows.

benchmark_categories.goal: Keep xy lightweight at import and smaller to install than broad plotting stacks.
benchmark_categories.metrics: cold import time, installed distribution bytes, file count
benchmark_categories.name: Install footprint and import budget
benchmark_categories.why: Notebook, CI, and serverless users feel package weight and cold import time before the first chart exists.

benchmark_categories.goal: Smooth exact WebGL scatter with bounded bytes/point and no JSON-number payload cliff.
benchmark_categories.metrics: FPS, TTFR, memory, bytes/point, hover latency
benchmark_categories.name: Medium direct scatter
benchmark_categories.why: Proves exact marker rendering, hover, color, and size channels before aggregation kicks in.

benchmark_categories.goal: Keep resident/render payload flat in N while showing truthful density summaries.
benchmark_categories.metrics: ingest/bin time, density payload size, peak memory, TTFR
benchmark_categories.name: Huge scatter overview
benchmark_categories.why: Proves screen-bounded rendering for datasets larger than the browser should draw point-for-point.

benchmark_categories.goal: Exact points when visible count is under budget; sampled/density with explicit counts otherwise.
benchmark_categories.harness: benchmarks/test_codspeed_kernels.py::test_adaptive_drilldown_cycle and ::test_adaptive_drilldown_cycle_mean_color (channel-bearing: per-request cost must exclude full-column color work)
benchmark_categories.metrics: visible-query latency, tier-switch latency, exact-point recovery, badge accuracy
benchmark_categories.name: Adaptive scatter drilldown
benchmark_categories.why: The large-data claim needs a credible path from overview to exact visible points.

benchmark_categories.goal: Screen-bounded line payloads with extrema-preserving decimation and fast zoom refresh.
benchmark_categories.metrics: decimation time, zoom re-decimation latency, TTFR, extrema preservation
benchmark_categories.name: Huge line/time series
benchmark_categories.why: Common observability and finance workload; Plotly-resampler sets the bar here.

benchmark_categories.goal: Measure the 10-60 chart scaling curve and expose LRU context eviction without discarding partial-row metrics.
benchmark_categories.metrics: payload prep, navigation readiness, per-chart setup/first draw, shader compiles/program links, startup long tasks, JS heap, redraw submission, scroll visibility, context loss/restore, stable chart-count ceiling
benchmark_categories.name: Many-chart dashboards
benchmark_categories.why: Plotly-class apps often fail from total page weight and many live canvases, not one chart.

benchmark_categories.goal: Stay responsive during interaction, avoid blank/flickering frames, then refine view after interaction settles.
benchmark_categories.metrics: pan/zoom FPS, wheel latency, hover latency, tooltip stability, selection latency, frame color delta
benchmark_categories.name: Interaction smoothness
benchmark_categories.why: Users judge performance by pan/zoom/hover, not just export time.

benchmark_categories.goal: Keep data payloads binary and screen-bounded where possible; warn when exact export would be huge.
benchmark_categories.harness: benchmarks/bench_vs.py, benchmarks/bench_scatter_native.py, benchmarks/bench_transport.py, benchmarks/test_codspeed_transport.py, benchmarks/test_codspeed_kernels.py::test_first_payload_density_large, benchmarks/test_codspeed_kernels.py::test_memory_report_density_medium, example app asset sizes
benchmark_categories.metrics: standalone HTML bytes, binary payload bytes, bundle bytes
benchmark_categories.name: Payload/export size
benchmark_categories.why: Notebooks, static HTML, docs, and dashboards pay for every byte shipped.

benchmark_categories.goal: Beat Plotly on user-visible first paint for common 2D charts while tracking Seaborn raster baselines where applicable.
benchmark_categories.harness: benchmarks/bench_2d_charts.py vs Plotly/Seaborn; benchmarks/bench_pyplot_vs_matplotlib.py; benchmarks/bench_interaction.py; CodSpeed core_2d rows
benchmark_categories.metrics: payload-prep time, payload bytes, standalone HTML bytes, TTFR
benchmark_categories.name: Core 2D chart breadth
benchmark_categories.why: The library needs to stay fast beyond the scatter wedge: bars, histograms, areas, and heatmaps are everyday chart workloads.

benchmark_categories.goal: Keep zero-copy inputs cheap and make unavoidable conversions visible.
benchmark_categories.metrics: ingest latency, copies, peak Python memory
benchmark_categories.name: Input ingestion
benchmark_categories.why: Real applications provide float32, strided, datetime, list, pandas, and Arrow inputs rather than only ideal contiguous float64 arrays.

benchmark_categories.goal: Keep stable-domain appends proportional to the batch and expose unavoidable domain-growth rebuilds.
benchmark_categories.harness: benchmarks/bench_workflows.py streaming rows; benchmarks/bench_transport.py append diagnostics
benchmark_categories.metrics: append latency, refresh bytes, incremental pyramid update latency, domain-growth rebuild latency
benchmark_categories.name: Streaming updates
benchmark_categories.why: Monitoring and notebook workflows append data repeatedly; stable domains should not trigger full-index rebuilds.

benchmark_categories.goal: Compute correct positive log domains from zone statistics with cost proportional to chunks, not points.
benchmark_categories.metrics: range latency, positive-domain correctness, peak Python memory
benchmark_categories.name: Log autorange
benchmark_categories.why: Large positive/negative and non-finite series are common in monitoring and scientific charts, and log axes must avoid full-data rescans.

benchmark_categories.goal: Keep polar payload prep bounded by composition size rather than observation count, and keep wedge subdivision proportional to each wedge's own angular span.
benchmark_categories.metrics: payload-prep time, wedge flattening cost, SVG/PNG export latency, inverse-raster latency
benchmark_categories.name: Polar coordinate system
benchmark_categories.why: Radar, wind rose, pie/donut and gauge views are a whole chart family, and a polar wedge is the most expensive mark in the engine — one annular sector per bar instead of one quad.

benchmark_categories.goal: Track each export target independently without mixing payload preparation and browser startup.
benchmark_categories.harness: benchmarks/bench_workflows.py export rows; benchmarks/bench_pyplot_vs_matplotlib.py matched PNG rows
benchmark_categories.metrics: export latency, output bytes, peak Python memory
benchmark_categories.name: Static export
benchmark_categories.why: HTML, SVG, and PNG export are common notebook, documentation, and reporting paths with different bottlenecks.
